text: Medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) establish T cell self-tolerance via autoimmune regulator (Aire) and peripheral tissue-specific self-antigens. RANK and CD40 signals crucially regulate mTEC development: RANK signaling alone was essential during embryogenesis, whereas postnatal establishment of the medullary microenvironment required CD40–RANK cooperation. Ligation of RANK or CD40 on fetal thymic stroma induced mTEC development in a TRAF6-, NIK-, and IKKβ-dependent manner. Separately, the first Aire+ mTECs emerged before αβ T cell repertoire selection, jointly directed by Rankl+ lymphoid tissue inducer cells and invariant Vγ5+ dendritic epidermal T cell (DETC) progenitors—the first thymocytes expressing gene rearrangement products. Aire+ mTECs then fostered Skint-1-dependent, Aire-independent DETC progenitor maturation, generating an invariant DETC repertoire. Thus developmental-stage-dependent RANK/CD40 cooperation and a Rank-mediated reciprocal DETC–mTEC link promote mTEC development, medullary microenvironment formation, and self-tolerance.
